title: The Last Garden Again
premise: Quentin Ravensworth has survived a decade in the magic-outlawed city of Corvane by being forgettable: a royal food-taster whose slow-built immunity to poison is her only secret, and whose small charms are sold so quietly that even she pretends they don't exist. When a dying stranger presses a map into her hands, Quentin learns the stranger was her mother's old ally—and that Quentin herself is the soul sold to the Undercourt beneath the mountain, collateral on a bargain made before her birth. To reclaim it, she must ally with Serah Vail, the court mage sworn to arrest her, and descend before the long winter seals the mountain for a generation. In the end Quentin wins back her soul by refusing to keep it whole—she splits it, leaving half to warm the imprisoned Undercourt and half to live free—choosing truth over loyalty to the crown that fed her, and love over the duty that would have kept her invisible.
about_author: P. M. Hartwell is the pen name of a former line cook who spent eleven years tasting other people's recipes before turning to fiction. Hartwell writes fantasy about small magics, large debts, and the people who keep cities fed.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A morning at the royal kitchens: she tastes the king's breakfast, detects almond bitterness laced with something worse, and quietly saves a steward's life while pretending nothing happened. Establishes her immunity, her hidden charm-selling, and her rule: never be noticed. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Charms for Quiet People
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Night market scene where she sells minor charms—a key that remembers locks, a candle that burns grief—to customers who never give real names. A city watchman, Doss, buys one and lingers too long. Emotional beat: tenderness traded carefully, the cost of staying unknown.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A bleeding stranger collapses into her rooms, presses a folded map into her hands, and dies whispering her childhood name—the one no living person should know. Watch bells begin to ring. Emotional beat: terror as the safe life cracks open.

chapters.title: What the Map Remembers
chapters.summary: Serah Vail's POV. The court mage investigates the death and finds traces of Quentin's magic; she withholds this from her superiors, unsettled by memories of a girl she once tutored. Introduces Serah's conflict between oath and conscience. Emotional beat: dread of what duty will demand.

chapters.title: Ten Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, flashback-woven. Fleeing through rooftops, Quentin recalls how her mother sold her soul to the Undercourt to buy the family's survival during the last famine winter. The map shows a route beneath the mountain. Emotional beat: grief reframing her whole life as an escape from a debt.

chapters.title: The Interrogation of Small Things
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah interrogates kitchen staff and charm-buyers, assembling Quentin's decade piece by piece, and realizes the crown itself may have known about the soul-bargain all along. She lies in her first official report. Emotional beat: the first deliberate betrayal of duty.

chapters.title: Doss Keeps a Secret
chapters.summary: Doss's POV. The watchman hides evidence that could condemn Quentin, torn between his badge and the woman who sold him a candle against grief. He passes her a warning through a market contact. Emotional beat: loyalty as a quiet, dangerous gift.

chapters.title: The Price of Almonds
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Cornered by the king's inquisitor, Quentin uses her immunity publicly for the first time—drinking poisoned wine meant to test a suspect—and walks away alive, now unmistakably marked as more than a taster. Emotional beat: invisibility ends; fear becomes resolve.

chapters.title: Two Oaths, One Road
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Ordered to hunt Quentin, Serah instead intercepts her outside the walls and offers a devil's alliance: help me learn what the crown buried, and I'll get you to the mountain. Emotional beat: wary trust kindling between enemies.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Begins
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. First snows fall early and wrong—too cold, too silent—as the Undercourt's influence leaks upward. Villages empty; charms fail. Quentin and Serah race the season toward the mountain pass. Emotional beat: the world itself turning hostile.

chapters.title: The Inn at Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Sheltering at a haunted inn, Quentin learns from its ghost-keeper how soul-bargains work: the Undercourt doesn't eat souls, it keeps them warm—and it is dying of loneliness. Emotional beat: horror softening into pity.

chapters.title: What Serah Buried
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Around the inn fire, Serah confesses she was the child who reported Quentin's mother to the authorities years ago, believing she was doing right. Quentin's fury nearly breaks the alliance. Emotional beat: truth as a wound that must be opened to heal.

chapters.title: The Pass of Teeth
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The mountain crossing: avalanches, a frozen river, and Doss appearing with supplies and a warrant he refuses to use. One companion must turn back; Doss stays behind to mislead the pursuit. Emotional beat: sacrifice without applause.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. They enter the Undercourt—a vast, lamplit cavern-city where the dead and the bargained-away linger. Its regent, the Pale Steward, greets Quentin like a long-awaited guest. Emotional beat: uncanny welcome, deeper unease.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Souls
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin finds her name in the Undercourt's ledger and reads her mother's full confession: the bargain bought not just survival but Quentin's protection from a worse creditor above ground. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as both debt and shield.

chapters.title: The Steward's Bargain
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. The Pale Steward offers Quentin her freedom if someone takes her place; Serah volunteers, citing her old guilt. Quentin refuses to let love become another transaction. Emotional beat: love refusing the logic of duty.

chapters.title: The Court Above Moves
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The king's inquisitor arrives through a sealed gate—revealing the crown has trafficked with the Undercourt for generations, feeding it souls to keep the winters short. Quentin's immunity was purchased the same way. Emotional beat: betrayal by everything she served.

chapters.title: Winter's Heart
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Quentin and Serah confront the inquisitor and the Steward together; the ledger burns, the mountain shudders, and the long winter accelerates as the ancient bargain unravels. Emotional beat: chaos as consequence.

chapters.title: Half a Soul
chapters.summary: Climax resolves. Quentin performs the forbidden rite: splitting her own soul, leaving half below to warm the lonely court forever, keeping half to live free above. The Steward weeps; the inquisitor's power breaks. Emotional beat: terrible, liberating choice.

chapters.title: The Thaw That Shouldn't Come
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. They climb out into impossible spring. Serah surrenders her badge and chooses exile beside Quentin rather than return to a crown built on stolen warmth. Emotional beat: relief braided with loss.

chapters.title: The Last Garden
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In her mother's ruined garden outside Corvane, Quentin plants seeds carried from the Undercourt's lamplit fields—flowers that glow faintly, half-alive with her given half-soul. Doss arrives, warrant finally torn. Emotional beat: quiet joy, roots after flight.

chapters.title: Again, From the Beginning
chapters.summary: Epilogue, shared POV. Years later, Quentin runs a garden-shop of honest charms and honest names; Serah teaches children the true history; each spring the flowers bloom brighter, as if the half below is dreaming well. Quentin tastes the morning air like a dish offered freely. Emotional beat: peace earned, inheritance transformed into gift.
